title: Fifty-electron bit read by repeated non-destructive skipper sampling
idea: MINIFY the stored charge ~600x (from ~30,000 e- to ~50 e-): the storage node is a ~0.01 fF floating diffusion with no capacitor, and a per-subarray skipper-CCD-style floating-gate amplifier shuttles the packet under its sense gate N=16 times, averaging read noise below 1 e- rms before write-back.
why: Deletes the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and the AR 60-75:1 etch; cell heads toward 4F2 and write CV2 energy falls ~100x. Only viable if node leakage is pushed to ~1e-21 A (pair with a wide-gap or pinned node).

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM with a tenfold smaller capacitor
idea: MINIFY temperature to 77 K: subthreshold and junction leakage drop >1e6, so retention reaches minutes even with Cs = 0.5 fF; capacitor AR falls from ~70:1 to ~7:1 and refresh nearly disappears, deployed as LN2-immersed rack sleds.
why: Hits facts 1 and 3 together: fewer high-AR steps (~20-30% cheaper cell process), refresh energy ~0; cooling overhead amortized at datacenter scale.

title: Latch-up as a feature: gated vertical thyristor bit
idea: Turn CMOS's classic failure into the storage mechanism: a vertical p-n-p-n stack in 1990s bulk silicon, 180 nm litho, with a capacitively coupled gate on its p-base latches into high-current on (1) or stays blocking (0); gate pulses set and reset it, and the read current is uA-scale with no capacitor.
why: Charge wall and sense signal (facts 1,8): no capacitor, read signal ~100x a DRAM cell, ~8F2 footprint; standby holding current or periodic refresh is the trade.

title: Janus coin: ferroelectric semiconductor channel that stores and senses itself
idea: Stimulus 'two-faced coin' -> use 2D alpha-In2Se3, a semiconductor whose own lattice polarization can flip, as the transistor channel; the polarization direction sets the threshold, so one device both stores and reads the bit with no capacitor and no separate ferroelectric gate layer.
why: 1T0C cell (~4F^2) removes the capacitor wall (fact 1) and destructive read (fact 8); low-temperature 2D transfer allows stacked tiers (fact 2).

title: Hole-confining SiGe quantum-well body for capacitorless 3D tiers
idea: Box = {medium: holes trapped in a compressively strained Si0.6Ge0.4 quantum well | access: lateral gate-all-around Si nanosheet | sense: threshold-shift read current (1T0C) | integration: 30-60 tier epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattice | substrate: Si | fab: one epitaxy run + staircase etch}. The ~0.35 eV valence-band offset forms a pocket under each nanosheet that holds holes written by impact ionization or GIDL, aiming for 100-1000x the retention of a homogeneous-Si floating body with no capacitor at all.
why: Fact 2: removes the capacitor that blocks 3D DRAM, so tier count rather than lithography sets density; target 4-8x bits/mm2 at 32+ tiers, built mostly with deposition and etch.

title: Origami artist: self-rolled Swiss-roll nanomembrane capacitor, plasma-ashed release
idea: An origami artist creates depth by folding a flat sheet. Deposit a flat, strained MIM stack on a polymer sacrificial layer; O2 plasma ashes the polymer away, and the released stack rolls itself into a ~10-turn Swiss-roll capacitor with 10-20x the capacitor area per footprint and no deep etch.
why: Breaks fact 1's charge wall at AR 60-75:1 without high-AR etch (fact 4). Dry release and no high-AR cleans mean more than 10x less water.

title: Charge-coupled serial memory tier for streaming camera frame buffers
idea: Edge cameras write and read frames sequentially, so bits are stored as charge packets in a CCD-style buried channel and clocked along gates with no per-bit access transistor or contact; random access happens at block granularity through a small SRAM head. Each bit occupies ~2-3F2 with no capacitor pillar.
why: Removes the access transistor, contacts and capacitor (facts 1-3) and most periphery (fact 7): 2-3x density for sequential tiers such as frame buffers or streamed KV caches; transfer efficiency and latency are the trade.

title: TSRAM fixed: hBN monolayer barriers make tunnel-diode latches reproducible
idea: TI's tunneling SRAM and 1960s Esaki-diode memories died because peak current depends exponentially on barrier thickness, so a one-monolayer deposition error broke the latch. Build each resonant-tunneling diode from an hBN/graphene/hBN stack whose barrier thickness is an integer layer count. A Goto pair of two series RTDs then holds a static bit at nA holding current with no capacitor.
why: Refresh-free static cell of ~8-10F2 vs SRAM's ~120F2; removes refresh energy (Fact 3) and the capacitor (Fact 1); variability is set by quantized layer count, not deposition drift.

title: Ferroelectric AlScN barrier toggles GaN 2DEG for gain-read memory
idea: Effect walk: spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization in wurtzite nitrides. A 5-nm ferroelectric AlScN barrier on GaN turns the polarization-induced 2D electron gas on or off depending on its switched polarity, giving a non-destructive gain read with ~10^4 on/off and no capacitor.
why: Runs on existing U.S. GaN/AlN fabs and 150-200 mm tools (U.S. manufacturability, capital intensity), and avoids the capacitor (fact 1) and destructive read (fact 8); AlScN's 3-5 MV/cm coercive field and wake-up/fatigue are the risks.

title: Williams tube's ghost: vacuum-nanogap access switch for temperature-proof retention
idea: Tube memories died from heaters, size and drift, but vacuum isolates charge perfectly. Gate each storage node with a 10-20 nm vacuum-gap field-emission switch carved in the BEOL and sealed at wafer level: its off-current is Fowler-Nordheim tunneling, essentially temperature-independent, not thermionic or generation leakage, so the femtoamp tail does not grow at 125 C.
why: Temperature-flat retention removes the ~8x refresh penalty silicon DRAM pays at 125 C (Fact 3); no channel material means no PBTI drift.

title: Intel 1103 three-transistor cell rebuilt on 22-nm FD-SOI back gates
idea: The first commercial DRAM (1103, 1970) was a 3T gain cell. Rebuild it on existing 22/28-nm FD-SOI lines with a thick-oxide write transistor held under reverse back-bias for sub-aA leakage and a thin-oxide read transistor whose back gate is pulsed only during reads for ~5x read current.
why: No capacitor (Fact 1); back-bias pushes retention to ~1 s (Fact 3: refresh energy down ~10-15x); non-destructive read removes write-back (Fact 8); existing non-EUV capacity.

title: Porphyrin redox monolayer giving multi-level charge per node
idea: Graft a monolayer of porphyrin or ferrocene molecules with 2-3 discrete oxidation states onto the storage-node electrode, combining molecular electronics with the DRAM capacitor so charge sits in molecular redox states at fixed potentials. Discrete states give quantized charge levels (2 bits/cell), and electrons must cross a molecular tether barrier to escape, stretching retention from 64 ms toward minutes.
why: Facts 1 and 3: 2 bits/cell plus up to ~1000x longer retention cuts refresh power; molecule stability over 1e15 cycles is the risk.

title: Printed redox-molecule monolayer storing quantized charge per molecule
idea: IFR: every molecule is an identical, perfect capacitor. Closest achievable: print a self-assembled monolayer of porphyrin or ferrocene molecules on printed electrodes; each molecule holds 1-2 electrons at sharp redox potentials, giving ~10 uC/cm^2 and natural multilevel states with seconds-to-minutes retention.
why: Fact 1: areal charge 10-100x an oxide capacitor, solution-printable; multilevel raises bits per cell.

title: Memory leasing with depot rejuvenation and retention re-binning
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: makers lease socketed DDR/CXL modules to hyperscalers and take them back every ~3 years; depots map retention, bulk-anneal to heal dielectric traps, re-bin by retention class and re-lease to less demanding tiers.
why: Usable supply: ~1.5-2x more service-years per wafer start during the 4x price spike; better capital efficiency.

title: Few-electron quantum-dot bit sensed by an adjacent single-electron transistor
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation taken to the limit: store each bit as ~5-10 electrons on a <3-nm Si or SnO2 quantum dot whose Coulomb charging energy (>100 meV) blocks leakage, and sense it non-destructively with an adjacent single-electron transistor whose current swings ~10x per electron.
why: Facts 1 and 10: ~1,000x less charge than a 5-fF cell, so CV2 write energy drops ~100x and no capacitor is needed; room-temperature dot uniformity is the risk.

title: Twenty-electron Coulomb island read by an in-cell single-electron sensor
idea: IFR: storing a bit needs only a few electrons. Closest achievable: hold ~20 electrons on a 3 nm silicon island whose Coulomb charging energy (>kT) blocks leakage, sensed nondestructively by an adjacent single-electron transistor whose current shifts a full period per electron.
why: Fact 1 disappears (required charge falls ~1000x) and so does fact 8 (destructive read); write energy drops to the aJ scale.

title: Gallium-oxide access transistor plus refresh-rate register cuts refresh 4x
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): keep the pins and protocol, and change only what the die reports. Replace the Si access transistor with a 4.8 eV beta-Ga2O3 vertical channel whose off current is ~1e-6 of Si so 5 fF holds for minutes, and have the die permanently report the slowest refresh-rate code already defined in the MR4 temperature/refresh register, so unmodified controllers issue 4x fewer REFs.
why: Uses an existing spec field to monetize retention: refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) down ~75% with zero controller change; Ga2O3 crystal quality at BEOL thermal budget is the risk.

title: Seed-regenerated tensors replace stored bits with recomputation
idea: Time-shift storage into computation: store a 32-bit PRNG seed plus a few coefficients per weight block, and regenerate weights on the fly in a near-memory generator at read time, so the bit lives as an algorithm.
why: DRAM demand: 3-8x fewer bits stored for compressible model weights, which raises usable supply without fabs.

title: Erasable conducting domain walls as non-destructive ferroelectric bits
idea: In thin-film z-cut LiNbO3-on-insulator, a field pulse injects a charged head-to-head domain wall between two electrodes that conducts ~uA, and a reverse pulse erases it. The read senses the wall current and never switches the polarization.
why: Read current is uA rather than fC, so reads are fast and non-destructive (fact 8). Walls are nanometers wide, so density is not capacitor-limited (fact 1), and nothing leaks (fact 3).

title: Erasable conducting domain wall in thin-film lithium niobate
idea: Worsen: read bits by dumping their charge onto a bitline, destroying them. Flip: store the bit as the presence or absence of a charged conducting domain wall in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa between two electrodes; a field pulse injects or erases the wall, and a small read voltage senses its >1000x conductance without moving it.
why: Non-destructive read removes restore energy and the overfetch penalty (fact 8: 5.9 pJ per useful bit); current-mode sensing shrinks sense-amp area (fact 7).

title: Z-RAM revived: SiGe quantum-well hole trap on bulk silicon
idea: Z-RAM died because holes stored in an SOI floating body leaked out through the junctions within milliseconds, and SOI wafers cost too much. Bury a 5-8 nm Si0.6Ge0.4 layer under a bulk vertical channel: its ~0.3-0.4 eV valence-band offset forms a hole well that keeps stored holes away from junction fields, and a p+ counter-doped floor isolates the body with no SOI.
why: Capacitorless 1T cell (~4F2) with an estimated 10-100x Z-RAM retention; removes the capacitor charge wall (Fact 1) and the SOI wafer cost; Ge is not a chokepoint.

title: Silicon-on-nothing vacuum-isolated membrane holds charge at 300C
idea: For hot users such as Venus probes and jet-engine controllers, one trench-array mask followed by a hydrogen anneal migrates silicon to seal an empty cavity under a thin Si membrane (empty-space-in-silicon process); the membrane is the storage body, isolated below by vacuum instead of junctions. Charge in the membrane modulates the overlying channel.
why: Removes the substrate-junction leakage component (fact 3) for 10-100x retention in a capacitorless cell (fact 1); one mask; membrane thickness uniformity is the risk.

title: BEOL complementary oxide latch: n-IGZO plus p-SnO cross-coupled
idea: Combine n-type IGZO with p-type SnO or Cu2O thin-film transistors into a cross-coupled CMOS latch built in the back-end and stacked 4-8 tiers over logic. Like SRAM it holds state statically with no refresh, but oxide off-currents (~1e-19 A) make standby power ~1000x lower than silicon SRAM.
why: Facts 3 and 2: refresh-free, monolithic 3D tiers over logic; lower density per tier than DRAM but multiplied by tier count; p-type oxide mobility is the risk.

title: Many-electron polyoxovanadate clusters as molecular storage nodes
idea: MAGNIFY electrons per site: a grafted monolayer of tungsten-free vanadium/molybdenum polyoxometalate clusters on the storage electrode accepts ~6-12 electrons each at discrete redox steps, so a 20-nm node holds ~10x the charge of a same-footprint dielectric capacitor and can encode several levels.
why: Faradaic pseudo-capacitance breaks the charge wall (fact 1) and avoids the tungsten chokepoint; the risk is electron-transfer kinetics slower than 100 ns.

title: Epitaxial all-perovskite SrRuO3/SrTiO3 capacitor without the interface dead layer
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: make electrodes and dielectric from one perovskite family (SrRuO3/SrTiO3/SrRuO3) grown coherently so no low-k interfacial dead layer forms; thin SrTiO3 then keeps k ~200+ instead of collapsing to ~50 as it does between TiN electrodes.
why: Fact 1: k~200 beats the k~70 target, so pillar AR could fall to ~20:1; low-temperature epitaxy on 3D surfaces is the risk.

title: Ferroelastic twin-variant bits read through strain-gated 2D channels
idea: Invert 'a bit is held as electrical or magnetic order' -> hold it as a crystal's shape. A ferroelastic film has two twin variants with orthogonal spontaneous strain; a piezoelectric AlN micro-actuator under each cell toggles the variant, and the strain state is read by the mobility shift of a 2D-semiconductor channel laminated on top.
why: No charge to leak (fact 3), non-destructive read (fact 8), diffusionless twin switching hints at very high endurance; nano-scale actuation and twin-wall pinning are speculative.

title: Mousetrap: strain-cocked ferroelastic twin variant holds the bit
idea: Stimulus 'cocked mousetrap' (stored elastic energy, two positions) -> a 20 nm ferroelastic perovskite pillar (e.g., LaCoO3-type) holds one of two twin orientations; a piezoelectric collar applies a ~1 ns shear pulse to flip the twin, and the variants' anisotropic resistivity (~2x) is read nondestructively along the pillar.
why: Non-charge storage with no refresh (fact 3) and nondestructive read that removes the restore cycle (fact 8); twin flipping moves no defects or ions, so endurance can be very high.

title: Coffee pod: storage-element wafers sold as bondable consumables
idea: Stimulus 'coffee pod' -> a dedicated, EUV-free line makes only the storage-element layer (dense capacitor or bit-element array on a thin carrier) and ships it as a consumable that logic or periphery fabs hybrid-bond face-to-face onto their CMOS wafers. Each layer runs on the cheapest line suited to it.
why: Splits DRAM capital: the bit-element fab needs no EUV transistor layers (fact 4) and the ~49% periphery runs in logic fabs (fact 7); claimed 30-40% capex per bit reduction and a U.S. entry point.

title: Qimonda trench reborn on a separate bonded capacitor wafer
idea: Qimonda's trench DRAM died because deep trenches competed with the transistor for area and thermal budget below 40 nm. Etch 100:1 trenches with porous-Si sidewalls (5-10x area) in a cheap blank carrier wafer, fill them with ALD high-k MIM, then hybrid-bond the carrier face-to-face onto the access-transistor wafer at cell pitch.
why: Decouples capacitance from the transistor process: 2-5x Cs (Fact 1), no pillar leaning, and the carrier needs no EUV (Fact 4). Risk: sub-100 nm bond pitch.

title: Bookbinding signatures: capacitors printed on a cheap 200 mm wafer
idea: Bind memory like a book: a U.S. 200 mm foundry prints the capacitor array as a separate 'signature' wafer, using i-line litho and Earth-abundant AAO or Ni/BaTiO3 capacitors, and sells it as a merchant product. It is wafer-to-wafer hybrid-bonded face-to-face onto transistor wafers from a leading-edge fab.
why: Fact 4 and U.S. manufacturability: ~40% of DRAM process steps move off EUV-class lines onto depreciated, idle 200 mm capacity, cutting capital per bit ~30%.

title: Freestanding epitaxial SrTiO3 membranes transferred as k-300 capacitor dielectric
idea: Scarcity rule: no dielectric with k below 100. Grow single-crystal SrTiO3/BaSrTiO3 on a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer, release wafer-scale membranes, and bond them onto the DRAM transistor array below 400 C; the dead-layer-free crystal keeps k ~300 at 10 nm so planar or 3:1 caps reach 5 fF.
why: Beats the k ~70 target (fact 1) 4x over, collapsing capacitor height and its HAR/EUV steps (fact 4); wafer-scale transfer and electrode interfaces are the risks.

title: Convert U.S. hard-disk read-head fabs to spin-memory element lines
idea: Combine the hard-drive industry's thin-film head wafer fabs in Minnesota, which already deposit and pattern TMR stacks at sub-30 nm, with back-end memory integration: contract them to make refresh-free magnetic storage-element wafers that are bonded onto CMOS periphery made elsewhere. As head volumes decline, the tools and TMR know-how convert to memory.
why: U.S. manufacturability and zero refresh: domestic, depreciated magnetic thin-film capacity instead of a new $15B fab.

title: Weak-retention dies resold as short-refresh AI memory
idea: Time-shift the binning: rather than scrapping dies that fail 64 ms retention, bin them by tail and sell them qualified at 16-32 ms refresh for AI accelerators that refresh aggressively anyway.
why: Scarce supply: recovers a few percent of wafer output as sellable bits with zero new fab capacity.

title: Charge-density-wave metastable state switched by picosecond electrical pulses
idea: Use the collective electron order of thin 1T-TaS2: a ~ps current pulse switches a nanoscale region from the insulating commensurate CDW into a metastable metallic 'hidden' state with 10-100x lower resistance. Confinement and strain engineering stretch its lifetime toward >=1 s at operating temperature.
why: The barrier is a collective electronic order (many electrons per nm3), giving ~fJ, ps switching with a non-destructive resistive read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Swap ionic ferroelectric for sliding-stacking ferroelectric tunnel barrier
idea: Use parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2 as an atomically thin tunnel barrier whose out-of-plane polarization flips when the layers slide by one-third of a unit cell. No ions move and no bonds break, so the cell should be fatigue-free, and the polarization modulates the tunnelling current for non-destructive read.
why: Turns endurance-limited ferroelectric memory into DRAM-endurance memory (>10^15 cycles targeted) at ~0.5 V (fact 10), and non-volatility removes refresh (fact 3).

title: NRAM's van der Waals idea, crystallized: sliding-ferroelectric bilayer bit
idea: NRAM's insight, a nanoscale state latched by van der Waals energy far above kT, was undone by random CNT fabrics. Keep the vdW latch but make it crystalline: a rhombohedral-stacked bilayer h-BN or 3R-MoS2 whose out-of-plane polarization flips when the layers slide by one bond length under a gate field, a lattice-locked stacking state that holds above 125 C.
why: Fatigue-free sliding switching with no ion displacement, an atomically thin nonvolatile cell at Grade 1, read via the threshold shift of an adjacent 2D channel.

title: Skyscraper sky-lobby bitlines enable 0.3 fF nodes in tall stacks
idea: Adapt sky lobbies, where express elevators stop at lobbies and local cars serve 16 floors: split each vertical bitline every 16 tiers with a local deposited-oxide sense amp, so each tier's node needs only ~0.3 fF against a short local bitline.
why: 10x at same cost: tiny capacitor-free nodes keep 128-tier stacks sensible; ~12x bits per footprint because the long-bitline capacitance problem is removed.

title: Ti: SnO2-seeded rutile TiO2 reaches k≈100 without ruthenium
idea: Use a 1-2 nm rutile SnO2 seed (isostructural, made of abundant tin) so ALD TiO2 crystallizes as rutile (k~90-170) at <=400 C instead of anatase (k~40), with ~1% Al doping to pin leakage; this replaces scarce Ru/RuO2 templates.
why: Delivers the k~70 escape route of fact 1, letting pillar AR fall from ~70:1 toward ~35:1 at the same 5 fF; cuts etch time and a scarce metal.

title: Optane endurance fix: monatomic antimony that cannot segregate
idea: Optane cells wore out after ~1e7-1e8 cycles as Ge, Sb and Te segregated and voids formed during repeated melt-quench. Use pure Sb confined to a 3-4 nm film inside a carbon/SiN pore: a single element has nothing to segregate, and nanoconfinement keeps the amorphous phase stable.
why: Endurance pushed toward 1e12+ with lower reset energy from the thinner film, keeping the 4F2 stacked crosspoint density.

title: Kalahari tracker: laser-crystallized improper-ferroelectric YMnO3 dots in blanket film
idea: A San tracker reads marks pressed into dry sand. Deposit a blanket amorphous YMnO3 film, then laser-crystallize only the cell sites into the hexagonal improper-ferroelectric phase; the amorphous remainder serves as isolation, so there is no etch or clean. Improper ferroelectrics keep their polarization at sizes where proper ones depolarize.
why: Lets a ferroelectric bit scale to tiny volumes (facts 1, 4). Write-by-light patterning needs no etch, strip or clean, a more than 10x water cut.

title: Pendulum clock: parametron phase bit sustained by one shared pump
idea: Stimulus 'pendulum clock' -> each cell is a GHz nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped parametrically at twice its frequency, so it can only oscillate at phase 0 or pi (Goto's 1950s parametron shrunk to NEMS); one global pump tone sustains every bit at once. Read compares phase with a reference; write injects a small seed signal as the local pump restarts.
why: Replaces row-by-row refresh with continuous collective sustain that steals no bandwidth (fact 3); no capacitor (fact 1); high-Q resonators need only ~aW per bit to stay alive.

title: Cold old node: 77 K planar-capacitor DRAM at 180 nm
idea: Reverse the scaling logic: run a 180 nm 1T1C array whose storage element is only a planar MOS capacitor (no trench, no stack) at liquid-nitrogen temperature, where junction and subthreshold leakage fall >1e6, so a 2 fF planar cap holds data for hours while the transistors gain mobility and steeper slope.
why: Capital and refresh (facts 3,4): a few-mask cell on depreciated tools with refresh gone; risk is shifting cost into system cooling.

title: Physarum oscillation-phase bit: nanomechanical parametron storing 0 or pi
idea: Slime mould encodes information in the phase of its cytoplasmic oscillations. Store each bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped ~1 GHz AlScN nanomechanical resonator: a 2f pump sustains either phase indefinitely, and a weak seed signal chooses which. Read by mixing with a reference phase on a shared line; many resonators share one pump line.
why: Replaces stored charge with phase, so there is no leakage tail, no refresh and no destructive read (facts 3, 8). AlScN is US-made and needs no EUV; energy scales with resonator Q (10^3-10^4).

title: Goto's parametron revived: bits as oscillation phase in pumped nanoresonators
idea: The 1950s parametron stored a bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped resonator; build rows of ~200-nm GHz NEMS beams (or compact LC tanks) driven at 2f by one shared row pump, so parametric bistability holds the phase while pumped and reading is a nondestructive phase comparison against a reference tone.
why: Facts 1 and 3: the bit is a dynamical state, not stored charge, so there is no capacitor and no refresh; pump power (~nW per high-Q resonator) beats 46 fJ/bit refresh only for Q>1e4, so it suits hot-buffer tiers rather than bulk capacity.

title: Swap one-physics capacitor for dual polarization-plus-charge two-bit cell
idea: Use a ferroelectric-dielectric capacitor that stores two independent bits: the polarization direction (non-volatile) and the linear charge magnitude (volatile). The read has two phases: a sub-coercive pulse senses the linear charge first, then a switching pulse with write-back senses the polarization.
why: 2 bits per DUV cell offsets the pitch loss from skipping EUV (fact 4), and the polarization bit survives power loss, so it can hold checkpoints.

title: Capacitor that shrinks on read: gated-diode voltage amplification
idea: Reverse the capacitor's role mid-operation: a 180 nm gated diode stores charge in its inversion layer; on read the gate is raised so capacitance collapses from Cox to Cdep, pushing the charge out as a 3-5x larger bitline voltage swing, built-in gain without a sense transistor.
why: Charge wall and periphery (facts 1,7,8): 3-5x less stored charge for the same signal, enabling planar storage, longer bitlines and fewer sense amps.

title: Antiferroelectric double-loop capacitor that buffers leakage with phase-transition charge
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric dielectric with the plate biased so writing a '1' crosses the field-induced AFE-to-FE transition and stores extra polarization charge (~10-20 uC/cm2). As the node leaks down to the backward-switching field, the polarization collapses and releases charge, clamping the node voltage like a reservoir; no remanence means no imprint or nonvolatility side-effects.
why: Fact 1: effective charge per area ~3-5x linear ZrO2 at the same voltage, and the built-in charge reservoir stretches retention 2-4x (fact 3).

title: Flytrap two-touch counter: analog leaky-integrator row-hammer sentinel
idea: The Venus flytrap counts touches with a decaying calcium signal and closes only after two touches within ~30 s. Give each row one extra storage capacitor that gets a fixed charge packet per activation and leaks through a calibrated transistor. When its voltage crosses a threshold, a comparator fires a targeted refresh of the neighbours, so per-row activation counting costs one cell's area instead of SRAM counters.
why: Row hammer (fact 9, flips at ~1k activations): per-row tracking at ~0.1% area, versus 1-3% for counter tables. The decay forgets benign accesses automatically.

title: Po: one capacitor, two opinions — coaxial nested-electrode two-bit pillar
idea: Po: a capacitor that holds two opinions. Extracted: build the pillar as a coaxial MIMIM (inner core, dielectric, middle tube, dielectric, outer shell); inner and outer capacitors are independent storage nodes reached by one transistor at the top and one buried at the pillar base.
why: Doubles bits per pillar footprint (fact 4) while reusing the existing high-AR etch. Coupling noise through the shared middle electrode is the risk.

title: Self-rolling Swiss-roll nanomembrane capacitors printed flat
idea: IFR: a capacitor that folds itself into 3D. Closest achievable: print a strained bilayer carrying dielectric and electrode layers on a sacrificial film; releasing it makes the stack roll into a multi-turn tube, multiplying plate area 10-50x per footprint.
why: Fact 1: high Cs from planar printing, no high-AR etch and no EUV.

title: Planar 1.5 fF capacitor rescued by stronger invisible on-die ECC
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): the host must see ordinary DDR5 data. Shrink the capacitor to a low-AR 1.5 fF cup that tolerates raw BER near 1e-5, and replace DDR5's internal SEC(136,128) with a hidden double-error-correcting code over 256-bit internal words (same ~6% parity) plus offset-cancelled sensing inside tRCD.
why: Spends invisible ECC and sense-time slack to delete the 60-75:1 pillar (fact 1) and several HAR/EUV steps (fact 4), ~20% lower wafer cost; partial-write read-modify-write must fit in tWR.

title: Carbon-cluster proximity gettering beneath every storage junction
idea: Borrow the image-sensor wafer makers' C3H5 cluster-ion implant: bury a carbon-rich gettering layer ~1 um below the array so Fe, Ni and Cu deep-level contaminants diffuse to it and lock away from storage junctions during anneals.
why: Fact 3: many tail bits are metal-induced generation centres; CIS white-pixel counts fell >10x with proximity gettering, so the 13 fA tail could shrink and refresh intervals stretch 2-4x at near-zero cost.

title: Eliminate excimer lithography: block-copolymer cylinders template every storage node
idea: Eliminate ArF and EUV exposure for the cell array, since excimer lasers need neon, argon and krypton and EUV drive lasers use helium: a high-chi block copolymer on a sparse UV-LED-exposed chemical guide self-assembles into a hexagonal 24-nm-pitch cylinder lattice. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O, N2 purge) turns the cylinders into AlOx hard masks for the storage nodes.
why: Removes 2-3 litho layers from the cell array (fact 4: 5-7 EUV layers today), and hexagonal packing fits ~15% more nodes per area; risk is reaching defect density under 1/cm2.

title: Sodium-potassium pump ratchet: AC-powered in-cell self-refresh
idea: Neurons hold their resting potential against leaks with a local ion pump, not a central refresh. Couple every storage node to a shared global AC pump line through a tiny asymmetric MIM tunnel diode in series with a node-gated diode. Each clock cycle pumps a few electrons toward whichever rail the node is nearer, so 1s are topped up and 0s drained without opening any wordline or bitline.
why: Refresh (fact 3): removes refresh activations, recovering the 10-20% of bandwidth and most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy. The pump current is pA per mat.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous ruthenium electrode inside every storage pillar
idea: Scale shift from battery-electrode science to the cell: deposit a Ru-Al alloy liner in the hole, selectively etch the Al to leave a 3-5 nm ligament nanosponge, then coat with ALD high-k and top electrode so one pillar has 3-5x internal surface area.
why: Capacitor wall: 3-5x Cs at the same footprint or same Cs at AR ~20:1, removing the hardest etch step.

title: Backside deep-trench storage capacitors under a frontside transistor array
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): same die footprint and pinout. After frontside transistors and periphery are built and bonded to a carrier, thin the wafer and etch storage trenches into crystalline Si from the backside (Bosch/cryo Si etch reaches 100:1), contacting each access transistor drain through the thinned body, which frees the frontside for periphery and bitline routing.
why: AR >100 in silicon (fact 1) decoupled from the transistor stack, with periphery congestion relieved (fact 7); reuses backside-power-delivery process know-how.

title: Long/short hedge: split-pillar dipole bit cancels common-mode leakage
idea: Like a market-neutral long/short position, store each bit as +Q/-Q on two halves of one pillar capacitor split by a vertical dielectric fin, accessed by twin transistors in the same active area; leakage and temperature drift hit both halves almost equally, so the difference decays far slower, and the sense amp compares the halves with no reference.
why: Facts 3 and 10: differential read doubles signal per pillar and tolerates ~3-5x more common-mode leakage, stretching refresh 4-8x; half-swing operation allows ~30% lower VARY for ~2x CV2 savings, at ~20% area cost versus 6F2.

title: Light-gated photoconductive switch isolating a dark capacitor
idea: Combine a wide-bandgap GaN thin-film photoconductor as the access switch with a storage capacitor: in the dark the switch is an insulator (~1e-20 A), and a nanosecond pulse from a row waveguide or micro-LED makes it conduct for write and read. With no electrical gate on the access path, the node holds charge for days without refresh.
why: Zero refresh and no 3 V wordline (fact 10), since the wordline is delivered as light; persistent photoconductivity is the risk.

title: Vacuum flask isolation: NEMS relay access switch with zero off-current
idea: A thermos blocks heat by removing the medium; block leakage the same way: connect the storage capacitor to the bitline through a ~200-nm TiN or poly-SiC cantilever relay in a sealed nanocavity, closed electrostatically by the wordline and open (vacuum gap) at rest, built with e-beam litho, sputtered TiN, sacrificial SiO2 and HF-vapor release.
why: Fact 3: off-state current is truly zero, so only capacitor dielectric leakage (~aA) remains and refresh nearly vanishes, and VARY is no longer tied to transistor Vt; contact wear and stiction (~1e10 cycles shown) are the risk for DRAM endurance.

title: NAND-style capacitor string sharing one transistor via threshold selectors
idea: Worsen: give each tiny capacitor its own expensive access transistor. Flip: stack 8-16 storage capacitors in a vertical string behind one access transistor, each gated by an ovonic threshold switch with staggered thresholds so the bitline voltage selects which capacitor charges or dumps.
why: 3D density without a lateral transistor per tier (fact 2); transistor count falls 8-16x and tiers are deposition-defined rather than litho-defined (fact 4).

title: Photonic-crystal nanocavity bistable bits for optical router packet buffers
idea: Optical packet routers want buffers that stay in the optical domain; InP or Si photonic-crystal nanocavities with carrier-induced bistability hold a bit at ~30-100 nW while light circulates and switch with fJ optical pulses. Placed beside co-packaged optics they cache data in flight without O-E-O conversion.
why: Targets data-movement energy (fact 5) in interconnect-heavy AI fabrics; density is low (~um2/bit), so it is a small fast tier, not bulk DRAM.

title: Sequential smart-cut stacking of single-crystal planar 1T1C tiers
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a planar trench-free MIM | access: lateral single-crystal Si FET in each transferred film | sense: SA on the base die | integration: 16-32 tiers by repeated hydrogen-implant layer transfer below 400 C | substrate: reusable donor wafers | fab: low-temperature bonding + splitting}. Each tier is a thin crystalline Si film with near-bulk access transistors, avoiding the poor poly or oxide channels that hurt monolithic 3D.
why: Fact 2: single-crystal channels in every tier remove the lateral-transistor blocker, and reused donor wafers keep substrate cost per tier small.

title: Po: a wafer is a napkin — remote-epitaxy peel-and-stack floating-body tiers
idea: Po: a wafer is a napkin you can peel. Extracted: grow 50 nm single-crystal Si films by remote epitaxy through graphene on a reusable donor wafer, peel and laminate 64 of them; each membrane carries capacitor-less floating-body cells defined by one imprint step, and each donor is reused ~100 times.
why: Avoids Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy and high-AR etch and amortises crystal cost over 100 reuses; 64 tiers with no EUV aims at ~100x $/GB. Trade-offs: bonding yield and tier-to-tier alignment.

title: Strain-switched magnetostrictive nanomagnet driven by sputtered piezo AlScN
idea: A sputtered AlScN piezo layer strains an elliptical FeGa nanomagnet, rotating its easy axis 90 degrees between two states that an MTJ reads. Write energy is the piezo's CV2 at 0.3-0.5 V (~1 aJ), with no current through the magnet and every film deposited at <=350 C.
why: ~100x below STT write energy (fact 10), with Galfenol avoiding rare earths and Pt, in a BEOL-stackable cell.

title: Charge-active, polarization-parked hybrid capacitor rows
idea: Combine a DRAM capacitor and a FeRAM capacitor in one ZrO2/HZO bilayer: rows in active use run as fast volatile charge cells, and when a row sits idle past ~10 ms the controller issues one plate pulse that copies its charge state into the ferroelectric polarization and powers the row down. Idle rows cost zero refresh, and the first access restores them to charge mode.
why: Fact 3: refresh energy on idle data (most of capacity) goes to zero with no change to active performance; ferroelectric wear is spent only per park (~1e6 parks/year).

title: Redox-molecule monolayers store quantized electrons on ITO glass
idea: Invert 'a capacitor holds a continuous amount of charge' -> store discrete electrons in molecules. A self-assembled monolayer of multi-state redox molecules (porphyrin or ferrocene triads) on ITO-coated glass holds 2-4 discrete oxidation states per site, giving up to 2 bits per cell at ~1e14 e/cm^2, read by redox current peaks at characteristic voltages.
why: ~10-20x the charge per area of a planar dielectric (fact 1), so no HAR capacitor, plus chemistry-defined multilevel cells; solid-state contacts, nanosecond kinetics and 1e15-cycle molecular stability are the risks.

title: Catalyst-etched 200:1 silicon capacitor holes using DSA mesh and Florida HF
idea: Box = {medium: charge on ALD dielectric in metal-assisted-chemically-etched Si holes | access: buried vertical FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C in bulk Si | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: U.S.-made block-copolymer DSA defines a Au/Ag catalyst mesh, then HF/H2O2 etches straight 200:1 holes}. The HF comes from fluorosilicic acid recovered at Florida phosphate plants instead of imported fluorspar, and the etch needs only wet benches, not imported high-AR plasma etchers.
why: Fact 1: AR beyond the 115:1 target without plasma-etch limits gives Cs ~10 fF or a tighter pitch, with low capital and fully domestic chemistry.

title: Po: memory is woven like cloth — drawn-fiber capillary-breakup storage nodes
idea: Po: memory is woven like cloth. Extracted: thermally draw a glass preform with a metal core and dielectric shell into km of fiber, then anneal so the core breaks into a chain of isolated nanospheres by Plateau-Rayleigh instability (each sphere a floating storage node); weave X and Y fibers so crossings capacitively address the spheres.
why: Fiber drawing yields km of nanostructure per hour with no lithography, cleanroom or EUV, targeting <1% of silicon's cost per area. Trade-offs: coarse addressing, us speed, a new interconnect scheme.

title: Movable-type memory: one standard storage-element socket, swappable bit physics
idea: Like Gutenberg's interchangeable type in one press, define an open hybrid-bond 'socket': a fixed periphery and sense wafer with a standard 0.5 um-pitch bond pad per sub-array plus fixed voltage, timing and signal windows. Any new storage-element wafer (capacitor, ferroelectric, magnetic) bonds on and is tested with no periphery redesign.
why: Fact 7 and capital intensity: a new bit physics becomes a wafer swap rather than a $1B program. Trial cost drops ~10-50x and the periphery stays on a mature node.

title: Eliminate the 64-ms retention spec: ephemeral sub-femtofarad cells for transient tensors
idea: Eliminate the assumption that every bit must survive 64 ms: build a memory class whose storage node is a planar ~0.5 fF capacitor with no pillar and ~100 us retention, used only for AI activations, KV-cache spill and gradients that are overwritten within microseconds; the controller tags allocations by lifetime and never refreshes them.
why: Removes the AR 60-75 pillar (facts 1, 4) for a large share of AI traffic; ~2-3x cheaper per bit for the ephemeral tier with zero refresh energy (fact 3).

title: Capacitorless 50-microsecond cells sized to transient tensor lifetimes
idea: Invert 'every bit must survive 64 ms' -> design a cell that only lasts ~50 us. A 2-transistor node using only the read-transistor gate capacitance (~0.1 fF, no capacitor) holds activations, gradients and attention scratch whose lifetime is microseconds; the compiler guarantees consumption or rewrite before expiry and hardware timestamps flag expired lines.
why: Removes the capacitor (fact 1) and all refresh for transient data, which is a majority of accelerator traffic; ~2-3x density over 1T1C on a logic-compatible process.

title: Po: a door opening to a secret knock — resonant-tunnelling floating node
idea: Po: a door that only opens for the right knock. Extracted: wrap the storage node in a Si/SiGe/SiO2 double-barrier stack whose resonant level aligns only at the write bias; at hold bias it is off-resonance and opaque (hours of retention), at write bias electrons pass resonantly in ns at low field without damaging the oxide.
why: Retention far beyond refresh needs with near-unlimited endurance (fact 3); a CMOS-material cousin of III-V UltraRAM. Barrier thickness uniformity is the risk.

title: Croconic acid proton-transfer ferroelectric bit
idea: Scale down to one hydrogen bond: in croconic acid crystals polarization flips by protons hopping between oxygens, giving room-temperature ferroelectricity at low coercive field from an organic, non-tungsten, low-temperature film.
why: Scarce resources and process: solution-processable bit layer near room temperature, sub-1 V target.

title: LCD chemistry: ferroelectric nematic liquid as a self-healing high-k dielectric
idea: Borrow display liquid crystals: fill a shallow cup capacitor with a ferroelectric nematic LC (RM734/DIO class, Ps ~6 uC/cm2, low-frequency permittivity ~1e3-1e4) confined in a 5-nm gap between alignment layers; as a liquid it cannot fatigue or crack, and breakdown spots self-heal by flow.
why: Fact 1 needs k~70; even if GHz-range permittivity is 10-100x below the static value, k>=100 cuts AR below 10:1; speculative because polarization response at ~10 ns in nanoconfinement and ionic leakage are unproven.

title: Ferroelectric nematic liquid-crystal capacitors filled like LCD panels
idea: Invert 'the capacitor dielectric must be a deposited solid' -> use a liquid. Ferroelectric nematic LCs (RM734/DIO class) show apparent permittivity of 1e3-1e4; display fabs capillary-fill them into nano-trench capacitors on glass with oxide-TFT access and seal them exactly as LCD lines do.
why: If even k_eff ~300 survives at nanosecond fields, 5 fF fits in a planar or AR<5 cell (fact 1) using idle Gen-8.5/10.5 display fabs (capital); risks are dielectric relaxation speed, interfacial artifacts behind the giant k, and ionic impurities.

title: Deliberately weakened canary capacitors trigger targeted per-mat rejuvenation
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying: place a few 'canary' copies of the storage element in every mat, built with ~20% thinner dielectric or smaller Cs so they age first; their retention, checked during refresh, triggers the heal action (anneal, detox pulse or spare swap) for that mat only.
why: Repairability: predictive maintenance instead of worst-case guard bands costing ~10-15% density or refresh energy.

title: DNA supercoil topology: polar-vortex chirality as a protected bit
idea: Supercoiled DNA keeps its linking number until an enzyme cuts and passes a strand. In lead-free BaTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice nanodots, store the bit as the clockwise or counter-clockwise chirality of a polar vortex, which is topologically protected against thermal flips. Asymmetric electrodes supply a curled field to switch it, and in dots where axial polarization is locked to chirality, the sign of the switched charge reads it.
why: Non-volatile at ~10 nm, where ordinary ferroelectric domains depolarize, so ferroelectric storage can scale below the ~20 nm FeRAM limit.

title: Polar-vortex handedness bits in oxide superlattices on scandate substrates
idea: Invert 'a ferroelectric bit is polarization up or down' -> store the chirality of a polar vortex. PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices grown on DyScO3 or SrTiO3 substrates form ~10 nm vortex tubes whose left/right handedness is a topologically protected binary state, switched by a curled field from twin gate electrodes and read by a chirality-dependent capacitance/piezo asymmetry.
why: Topological protection gives retention and disturb immunity at ~10 nm pitch (density, fact 9) with no capacitor; electrical chirality read/write at speed is unproven.

title: Polar flux-closure vortex chirality as a sub-5 nm ferroelectric bit
idea: In PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice nanodots, polarization curls into closed vortices that carry no surface bound charge, so the depolarizing field vanishes. Store the bit as vortex chirality (clockwise or counterclockwise), written by a curled field from an offset electrode pair and read through the chiral piezo or tunneling signal.
why: Ordinary ferroelectric bits fail below ~10 nm because depolarization energy beats the barrier; closure textures delete that term. Aims at a 3-5 nm polar bit (density) with no charge leakage (fact 3).

title: Zuse Z1 sliding-plate memory as nanomechanical detented shuttles
idea: Zuse's 1938 Z1 held bits as the position of sliding metal plates with pins. Fabricate 200-nm Si or TiN shuttles in BEOL cavities with a buckled-beam double-well detent, set left or right by an electrostatic comb pulse and read by differential capacitance to a sense line.
why: Bit is a mechanical position: non-volatile, zero leakage, contact-free so effectively unlimited endurance (Fact 3); ~10 ns switching at this size; ~20F2 cell but zero refresh energy.

title: 1950s diode-capacitor store reborn as stacked selector-capacitor crosspoint decks
idea: Early machines held bits on capacitors gated by diodes rather than transistors. Revive it as 1S1C: planar MIM capacitors stacked with a two-terminal ovonic or punch-through selector (~1e-15 A off) in BEOL decks, accessed by V/2-biased crosspoint lines with short 64-cell bitline segments so ~0.5 fF suffices.
why: No lateral transistor and no high-AR pillar (Facts 1, 2): 4F2 per deck x 4 decks in BEOL; refresh interval set by selector leakage rather than junction tails.

title: T-RAM thyristor latch revived on existing SOI production lines
idea: T-RAM Semiconductor's thin capacitively-coupled thyristor (abandoned around 2010) held bits as the latched state of a gate-coupled pnpn device. Re-target it to existing 22FDX and 45-nm PD-SOI flows, using modern back-bias to cut standby current and ALD gate dielectric to tighten the coupled gate.
why: Regenerative bistable storage in ~10F2 with ~1 ns reads and large read current, no capacitor (Fact 1), and only pulse-refresh every few seconds (Fact 3); entirely existing SOI capacity.

title: Relay-computer revival: NEM pull-in hysteresis latch at zero current
idea: Relay and neon-lamp memories held bits inside a hysteresis window between pick-up and drop-out. In existing MEMS foundries or 180-nm BEOL, build TiN or poly-Si cantilever relays biased between their pull-out (~1.5 V) and pull-in (~3 V) voltages, so a pulled-in beam stays in and a released beam stays out at zero DC current.
why: Static storage with zero leakage through an air gap (Fact 3), abrupt selector-like on/off, no capacitor; ~1 um2 cells make a low-power state store built entirely in existing MEMS capacity.

title: Drum memory reborn: stationary disk media scanned by head arrays
idea: Drum memories held bits on a moving magnetic surface under fixed heads. Invert it: existing HDD media sputter lines coat granular CoCrPt on Si, and existing HDD head fabs build 1000-head arrays on a MEMS x-y stage (+-50 um), each head owning a micro-field of media.
why: ~1 Tb/in2 media density with no lithography per bit; us access and massive parallel bandwidth make a DRAM-offload capacity tier (cold KV caches, embeddings) built on under-used HDD capacity.

title: Split-pillar complementary capacitor in one etched hole
idea: Etch a single capacitor hole, then split its bottom electrode lengthwise into two half-shells separated by a dielectric fin, so one hole holds a true and a complement storage node sharing one plate. Complementary charges give a differential 2x signal that cancels plate and coupling noise.
why: Fact 1: 2x sense margin per hole lets each half carry ~40% less charge (shorter pillar); differential sensing also improves row-hammer tolerance (fact 9).

title: Roll-to-roll anodized aluminium foil gives 150:1 capacitor pores free
idea: IFR: high-aspect holes that etch themselves. Closest achievable: anodize aluminium foil on a reel so self-ordered alumina pores grow ~20 nm wide and ~3 um deep (AR ~150) with no lithography, then spatial-ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside to form capacitor arrays laminated onto access-device layers.
why: Facts 1 and 4: passes AR 115 with zero EUV and zero plasma etch, on abundant aluminium.

title: Shadow-latch cell that hands its bit to a nonvolatile twin
idea: Worsen: keep refreshing billions of idle bits all night. Flip: pair each DRAM cell group with a tiny ferroelectric tunnel-junction shadow element; when a bank goes idle its bits are copied into the shadows in one burst, refresh stops, and the bits are restored on wake.
why: Idle refresh energy (16-33% of idle power, fact 3) drops to near zero while active speed stays DRAM-class.

title: Quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 makes planar storage capacitors at 77 K
idea: Effect walk: quantum paraelectricity. Below ~100 K, SrTiO3 (or KTaO3) permittivity climbs into the thousands because quantum fluctuations suppress the ferroelectric transition, so a 10-nm epitaxial film on a planar cell stores 5 fF in a small fraction of today's area; at 77 K the access-transistor leakage tail also drops by >10^6.
why: Answers the capacitor wall (fact 1 needs k~70; STO offers k~1000+ cold even after thin-film dead-layer losses) and removes refresh (fact 3) for liquid-nitrogen-cooled AI memory pools, with no AR-60 etch; cooling costs ~10 W wall power per W removed.

title: Quantum anomalous Hall edge chirality as a dissipationless cryogenic bit
idea: Effect walk: quantum anomalous Hall effect. In a MnBi2Te4 or Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 micro-Hall cell at 2-10 K, magnetization sets which way the dissipationless edge channel circulates; read senses the Hall-voltage sign at sub-mV, and write uses the topological insulator's own giant spin-orbit torque.
why: Read dissipation approaches zero (quantized, backscatter-free), which matters where every nW at 4 K costs ~1 W at room temperature: >=10x lower system energy per access than shipping data to warm DRAM for quantum-control and cryo-compute stacks.

title: 3D core memory: deposited magnetic rings threaded by vertical vias
idea: Core memory died because millimetre ferrite cores had to be threaded by hand. Deposit alternating CoFeB-ring/dielectric tiers as 3D NAND does and etch one vertical metal pillar through each ring stack: coincident currents in the pillar and a tier plate line flip one ring's vortex chirality, and a TMR sensor on each tier reads it.
why: 3D density from one etch with no lateral transistor per tier (Fact 2); nonvolatile, and closed-flux rings do not couple even at tight pitch.

title: DX-centre persistent photoconductivity: light writes, lattice barrier holds
idea: Effect walk: photoconductivity with large lattice relaxation. A waveguide photon pulse ionizes DX-type deep donors in a channel (AlGaAs:Si-like centres re-engineered in a wide-gap host with a >=0.9 eV capture barrier) into shallow donors, raising conductance; the configurational barrier keeps electrons free, and a hot-electron gate pulse recaptures them to reset.
why: Holds the bit in a lattice-relaxation barrier instead of leakage-limited charge, targeting refresh-free retention (fact 3) and an optical write path that bypasses wordline drivers (fact 7); known DX hosts only retain below ~100 K, so a new host is required.

title: S: tetrathiafulvalene rotaxane monolayer crossbar with defect-mapped molecular switches
idea: Sandwich a monolayer of bistable [2]rotaxanes between nanoimprinted crossbar wires at ~15 nm pitch; oxidizing the sulfur-rich tetrathiafulvalene station shuttles the ring and changes junction conductance, and a defect map plus code tolerates ~1% dead or shorted junctions.
why: Crossbar of molecules gives ~4F² density with no per-bit transistor or EUV (fact 4); switching speed (us-ms) and endurance are the gap to DRAM-class, so it starts as a dense slow tier.

title: Pinned-photodiode buried node borrowed from image-sensor foundries
idea: MAGNIFY retention by holding the bit in a fully depleted, surface-pinned buried n-well (a CIS pinned photodiode kept dark, dark current ~1-10 e-/s) with a transfer gate and source-follower readout like a global-shutter pixel memory, taped out on a commercial CIS MPW.
why: Retention of seconds to minutes at ~2,000 e- cuts refresh energy and bandwidth >100x (fact 3) on a known foundry process; ~0.5-1 um2 cells suit low-power embedded tiers.

title: Swap litho-defined cells for thickness-defined annular capacitors in stacks
idea: In a 64-pair Si/SiGe stack, etch one DUV hole per cell column and selectively recess the SiGe laterally into ring cavities whose height is set by film thickness (~8 nm). ALD fills them as ring capacitors, each wired to the lateral transistor in its tier.
why: Solves the 3D capacitor blocker (fact 2): deposition thickness, not lithography, sets the critical dimension, so 64 tiers need one DUV litho step (fact 4).

title: Po: the bit is a border — conductive ferroelectric domain-wall memory
idea: Po: the bit is not the country but its border. Extracted: in thin LiNbO3 or BiFeO3, write or erase a charged domain wall across a nano-gap; the wall conducts 1e3-1e6x more than the bulk, so the bit is wall present/absent, read non-destructively by a small current.
why: Non-destructive read removes restore energy (fact 8) and refresh (fact 3). Wall pinning and drift reliability are the risks.

title: Gated-diode amplifying storage node that boosts its own signal
idea: Box = {medium: charge in a Si gated-diode (MOS varactor) node | access: one Si FET | sense: on read the gate is pulsed so the varactor drops from inversion to depletion capacitance (~5x lower), raising node voltage ~5x before charge sharing | integration: planar 2T-class cell | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: standard domestic CMOS with no high-k capacitor}. The storage element amplifies itself (Q fixed, C collapses), so the cell needs only ~1 fF and no pillar.
why: Fact 1 and capital: removes the high-AR capacitor and its dielectric, so the cell can be built on existing domestic logic lines.
